predecessors.name: Kingdom of the Franks
predecessors.text: Aquitaine and 'the rest as far as Spain', assigned to Charles the Bald at Verdun

successors.name: Kingdom of France
successors.text: the Capetian kingdom: the page names the Kingdom of France as West Francia's successor

ledger.x: 843: the Treaty of Verdun creates West Francia for Charles the Bald.
851: Brittany wins de facto independence.
867: Salomon of Brittany is granted the counties of Avranches and Coutances.
869: Charles the Bald has himself crowned king of Lotharingia at Metz.
870: Wilfred the Hairy becomes count of Urgell and Cerdanya.
870: Meerssen ends the contest for Lotharingia (8 August).
870: the Treaty of Meerssen (8 August) gives Charles the west of Lothair II's realm.
872: the men of Pallars and Ribagorza break away from Toulouse.
872: the men of Pallars and Ribagorza break away from Toulouse.
876: after Louis the German's death (28 August) Charles the Bald invades East Francia.
876: 8 October, Charles is 'decisively beaten at the Battle of Andernach'; no ground is kept.
877: Provence comes under the Carolingian crown.
878: Wilfred receives Barcelona, Girona and Besalú.
879: Boso founds the kingdom of Lower Burgundy and Provence.
880: Louis III and Carloman II take Mâcon and the north of Boso's realm.
880: Ribemont gives western Lotharingia back to East Francia.
882: Boso's remaining realm falls.
887: Charles the Fat confirms Louis the Blind in Provence.
888: Aquitaine breaks away.
888: Odo, a Robertian, is crowned king at Compiègne.
889: Ranulf of Aquitaine submits to Odo.
896: Cliopatria's West Franks shape takes in Aquitaine (824 cells) the year its own Aquitaine row ends.
898: the Carolingians return.
911: Rollo receives the land around Rouen.
911: Lotharingia turns to Charles the Simple.
922: Robert I, Odo's brother, is crowned by the rebels.
923: Rudolph, Duke of Burgundy, is elected king after Robert I's death.
923: Henry the Fowler invades Lotharingia.
924: King Rudolph extends Rollo's county westward.
925: the Lotharingians choose Henry.
925: Lotharingia passes to East Francia (Henry the Fowler).
926: Cliopatria adds the other 56 cells (Orne 21, Eure 20, Manche 7, Mayenne 2, 6 elsewhere) to its Duchy of Normandy at West Francia's expense; no opened page names them.
936: Louis IV restores Carolingian rule.
987: Hugh Capet is elected king and the Capetian dynasty begins.
989: the dossier ends; Aquitaine's nominal homage is carried to the Kingdom of France dossier.
989: West Francia ends as the Kingdom of France begins in Cliopatria (990).

wars.name: Breton revolt and the Battle of Jengland
wars.outcome: 'The Bretons were successful in obtaining a de facto independence' under Erispoë.

wars.name: Partition of Lothair II's kingdom (Treaty of Meerssen)
wars.outcome: Charles the Bald is crowned at Metz in 869; the partition of 8 August 870 gives him the west, Lyon and Vienne and part of Upper Burgundy including Besançon, and Louis the German the east with Aachen and Metz.

wars.name: Charles the Bald's invasion of East Francia
wars.outcome: Charles attacks after Louis the German's death (28 August 876) and is 'decisively beaten at the Battle of Andernach on 8 October 876'.

wars.name: Carolingian war against Boso
wars.outcome: Boso takes Lower Burgundy and Provence in 879; 'Boso suffered several territorial loses, but still kept his kingdom'; Vienne falls in September 882.

wars.name: Louis the Younger and the treaty of Ribemont
wars.outcome: Louis the Younger is invited to West Francia in 879 and, 'in February 880' at Ribemont, receives 'the western half of Lotharingia'; Louis III and Carloman II are recognised in the rest.

wars.name: Siege of Paris
wars.outcome: Sigfred's fleet sails up the Seine in 885; Charles the Fat camps at Montmartre in 886 and, when the Vikings withdraw, pays them '700 pounds of promised silver'.

wars.name: Odo and Charles the Simple
wars.outcome: Fulk crowns the 14-year-old Charles at Reims in 893; Arnulf recognises him in 894 and returns to Odo in 895; in 896 Odo cedes part of the realm and makes Charles his successor; Odo dies 1 January 898.

wars.name: Rollo's settlement (Treaty of Saint-Clair-sur-Epte)
wars.outcome: Rollo is given the land west of the Epte, 'broadly Rouen and the area of present-day Upper Normandy', in return for baptism and vassalage; Dudo of Saint-Quentin, a century later, is the source of the terms.

wars.name: Charles the Simple, Henry the Fowler and Lotharingia
wars.outcome: Lotharingia switches to Charles in November 911; the Treaty of Bonn (7 November 921) recognises him; Henry invades in 923 and the Lotharingians elect him in 925.

wars.name: Louis IV and Otto I over Lotharingia
wars.outcome: Gilbert's rebellion (936) and Louis IV's marriage to his widow keep a West Frankish claim alive; Otto defeats Gilbert at Andernach (939), accepts homage from Hugh the Great and Herbert II at Attigny (942) and meets a West Frankish invasion in 944 with a large…

wars.name: Lothair's Verdun campaign
wars.outcome: No border moved on the page or in Cliopatria.

certainty.note: Borders are approximate: the Meerssen line of 870 ('ran roughly along the rivers Meuse, Ourthe, Moselle, Saone and Rhone') is the only described frontier, and Brittany, the Spanish March and Aquitaine are marches.

The East Frankish frontier fixed at Ribemont in 880 'remained largely the same until the Late Middle Ages' (Ribemont page) but is not described by lines; Aquitaine, Normandy, Brittany, Flanders and Burgundy are autonomous principalities…
